To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the synthesis, characterization, and biological evaluation of some amino and carbony analogs of the galactose-containing oligosaccharide 2-(trimet-hysilyl)ethyl alpha-D-galacto-pyranosyl-(1-->4)-beta-D-galactosyl-1-thio-beta-D-galactose (1), a potent inhibitor of the binding of PapGJ96 to its receptor (Galalpha1-->4Galalpha1-->O-S

the 2'-amido, the 6-amido, and the 6-carboxyl analogs of 2-(trimeth-ylsilyl)ethoxy (alpha-D-ga-lactopyranosyll)-(1-->4)-(ss-D-gal-actopyranosid) were evaluated as inhibitors of PapGj96 binding to the Gal alpha 1-4Gal epitope, using an ELIS A assay.

the 6-carboxymethyl and 6-carbo-xy analogs of the galabioside inhibitor were inactive, while the 2'-amido- and 6-amido analogs were potent, supporting the combining site model, which includes a negatively charged aminoacid residue near the hydroxyl groups of the galabiol.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design, synthesis, and evaluation of inhibitors of the binding between the pilus protein of uropathogenic Escherichia colii and the galabiose-containing receptor on the surface of human erythrocytes.

the synthesis of some amino and/or carboxy analogues of the reference inhibitor 2-(trimethysilyl)ethyl alpha-D-galacto-pyranosyl-(1-->4)-beta-D-galactoside, and the evaluation of the inhibitory efficiency of these analogs towards the binding of PapGj96.
the synthesis and evaluation of a series of galactose-containing compounds that may be useful as inhibitors of bacterial infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 2'-hydroxyl group is essential for the inhibitory effect of the galabioside, whereas the 6'-hydroxyl is not.
the amino analogs are more potent inhibitors than the carboxy analog.

the combining site is located on the surface of PapGj96 and is composed of a hydrophobic pocket, a hydrophilic pocket, and a negatively charged pocket, and that the galabiose moiety of the inhibitor is located in the hydrophobic pocket and the hydroxymethyl group of the 2'-deoxy-2'-amino group is located in the negatively charged pocket.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 2'-amido group in the reference inhibitor is not essential for inhibition of PapGj96 binding, whereas the 6'-amino group is essential, and the 6'-carboxy group is deleterious.
the 2'-deoxy analogs are better inhibitors than the 2'-amido analogs, and the latter are better than the 2',6-dideoxy analogs.

a galabiose-based inhibitor with a carboxy group at the C-6 atom is a poor inhibitor, but that the 2'-ammino and 6-amino analogs are promising inhibitors, which should be further evaluated in a biological assay.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 6-carboxylate is an important group for the inhibitory activity of these compounds.
the 2-amino-2-deoxy and 6-car-boxy groups of the reference inhibitors are important for binding.
the 6-carboxylate analog of the galabioside is a poor inhibitor, which is in line with the proposed model.
